name: CWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The federation's top singles belt, added in its opening months of 2003. Its own pages name Christian Cage the first World champion of the second run and Faith the first woman to hold it, with Priest champion on both surviving broadcasts; its last broadcasts date his hold on it both to May and to September, with X-Factor's win at Bloodbath between.

name: CWF International Championship
epitaph: Created at the first Aggression of the second run, on 12 September 2004, and first awarded in a battle royal to Ryan Coleman. Dark Rayne's undefeated reign is billed as the longest; the surviving broadcasts show it passing from Fuel to Christian Connolly at Genocide and from X-Factor to The Punk at Ultimate Chaos.

name: CWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Added in the federation's first months in 2003 and held in the second run by Talent Inc among others; the surviving broadcasts have the Hit Squad champions at Genocide and Generation Xtreme champions by Ultimate Chaos.

name: CWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: A belt for men of 225 pounds or under, added in 2003; Michael Machete is champion on both surviving broadcasts and defends it against Ken Sandwave and Carnage and then against Neptune.

name: CWF Women's Championship
epitaph: Its own title-history page opens with Faith, who beat Roxie Michaels at Shockwave on 15 March 2005, then Dana Morris on 1 May 2005; the surviving broadcasts show Syd Ashley taking it from Faith in a gauntlet at Genocide and Faith holding it again by Ultimate Chaos.

name: CWF Chaos Championship
epitaph: An anything-goes, no-holds-barred belt created at the first Aggression of the second run and awarded to Jason Garret, held under a 24/7 rule that let it change hands anywhere; its own About page names Jake Fury, Cenotaph, Faith, Violent A and Priest among its holders.

name: CWF Television Championship
epitaph: Introduced in the federation's opening month, January 2003; Violent A is its former champion on the last Ultimate Chaos and Nemesis was the first man to hold it together with the Tag Team title.

name: CWF United States Championship
epitaph: Added in 2003 after the Television title; Jake Fury's own Hall of Fame page has him battling Souless for it in the federation's first year.

name: CWF Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The last of the first year's belts, added in 2003 after the Cruiserweight title according to the federation's own About page.
